Representatives of the Andhra Pradesh Adventure Sports Academy (ASA) and the National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports (NIMAS), functioning under the Union Ministry of Defence, after signing an MoU, at the Secretariat on Friday. | Photo Credit: HANDOUT
Andhra Pradesh is aiming to position itself as a leading adventure tourism destination in the country, with Gandikota set to emerge as a major adventure sports and training hub in South India.
As part of its efforts to promote adventure tourism, develop youth skills and generate local employment opportunities, the Andhra Pradesh Adventure Sports Academy (ASA) signed an MoU with the National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports (NIMAS), functioning under the Union Ministry of Defence. The partnership deal was signed by NIMAS Director Colonel Ranveer Singh Jamwal and ASA Secretary Unnadi Raghunath Reddy at the Secretariat on Friday in the presence of Tourism Minister Kandula Durgesh and senior officials S.S. Rawat and Amrapali.
As part of the collaboration, professional training would be provided to local youth to develop them into certified adventure guides, instructors, rescue personnel and outdoor leaders. The first combined Basic and Intermediate Paramotor Courses will be conducted at Gandikota from January 6 to 31, 2027, under NIMAS technical supervision. Training will cover ground techniques, equipment handling, safety procedures and flying instructions.
The collaboration will subsequently expand to trekking, rock climbing, wilderness first aid, kayaking and water rescue. ASA is also expected to function as a regional NIMAS-affiliated training centre for South India, opening up new career opportunities for aspiring adventure sports enthusiasts.
In another initiative to promote Gandikota’s historical heritage and fitness tourism, the Tourism department will organise a ‘Gandikota Run-2026’ on December 27. Organised jointly by ASA and Go Heritage Runs, the event will feature 3-km fun runs and 5-km and 10-km races, with around 1,000 participants expected to participate. Runners have been advised to reach Gandikota on December 26 to collect their bibs. Registrations are open through the websites www.asaao.org and www.ifnish.com.
Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (APTDC) is planning to expand its tourism activities across the state. Operating 42 boats at nine locations in six districts, besides managing the Srisailam ropeway, Belum Caves and Borra Caves, APTDC recorded over 27 lakh tourist visits and an operational surplus of ₹15.70 crore during 2025-26.
Nine control rooms will monitor tourist safety across the state. The APTDC board has also approved the purchase of two 50-seater FRP boats and four speed boats at a cost of ₹1.40 crore. A Water Sports Training Institute is being proposed at Mangamaripeta in Visakhapatnam to provide professional training to personnel.
With the introduction of these proposed initiatives, the government aims to strengthen tourism infrastructure, encourage private investment, generate employment and establish Andhra Pradesh as a prominent adventure tourism destination in India.
